items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The American musicians presented at this festival were ... and myself. ... France was represented by ... Lucien Simoens ...

ctx.x: The 18th of October Willie Lewis and his orchestra recorded six numbers with the full band. The 12th of November I recorded under my own name with Stephane Grappelli, Joseph Reinhardt on guitar, Wilson Meyers and Ted Fields, drums. Grappelli surprised me by playing piano on some of the numbers. Whenever Hugues Panassie asked me to record I seldom asked who the other musicians would be unless I was asked to choose them. And that was the reason I was surprised when I arrived at the studio and I knew the instruments…

November the 19th I recorded "Bill Coleman Blues" accompanied only by Django on guitar which was another first for Hugues Panassie because it was his idea to record just the two of us for one number and it was the first time a trumpet and guitar had been recorded on a jazz record. The other five numbers recorded on that date had Christian Wagner clarinet and alto, "Big Boy" Godie tenor and clarinet, Emil Stern, piano, Lucien Simoens, bass, and Jerry Mengo drums.

After the engagement at the Paris Fair, Willie Lewis and orchestra were engaged to go to Alexandria, Egypt and this was as thrilling as the trip to India. I had seen Egypt for a few hours going and coming from India and now it was possible for me to spend some weeks there. I was now a papa because Joan was with Beezie and I. The musicians that were married took their wives with them. But Jack Butler's wife had gone back to the States and "Big Boy Goodie" was a batchelor. Willie Lewis was married also but his wife…
